subtitle: A feudatory remakes the Deccan through steel, inscription and sacred rebirth

panels.shot: towering low-angle hero wide with ritual backdrop
panels.action: Dantidurga stands in ornate early-medieval armour before a shadowed Vedic fire altar and a gleaming golden vessel, the basalt cliffs of Ellora and the Deccan plateau stretching behind him under a storm-dark sky.

dialogue.text: In the eighth-century Deccan, Dantidurga, Rashtrakuta lord, steps through a golden womb to cast off his past and be reborn as king.

i18n.hi: आठवीं सदी के दक्कन में दंतिदुर्ग, राष्ट्रकूट स्वामी, स्वर्ण गर्भ में उतरकर अतीत छोड़ राजा रूप में फिर जन्म लेता है।

panels.shot: high aerial establishing shot
panels.action: A sweeping view of the Deccan plateau shows scattered fortified towns, winding rivers and dry fields, with tiny armies and caravans moving between them under a hazy sun.

dialogue.text: The mid-eighth century Deccan was a land of plateaus and passes, of old dynasties and new warlords, where power rode with horsemen and flowed with the monsoon rivers.

i18n.hi: आठवीं सदी का दक्कन पठारों‑दर्रों, पुरानी राजवंशों और नए सेनानायकों की धरती था, जहां शक्ति घुड़सवारों के साथ दौड़ती और मानसून नदियों के साथ बहती।

panels.shot: mid-wide of a Chalukya court
panels.action: Inside a Badami Chalukya hall, nobles in rich garments sit beneath carved stone beams, while a central throne stands slightly raised, its occupant implied but not shown.

dialogue.text: For generations, the Badami Chalukyas had held this high ground, ruling from their red-stone strongholds, commanding feudatories in all directions.

i18n.hi: पीढ़ियों से बादामी चालुक्य इस ऊँचे भूभाग पर जमे थे, लाल पत्थर के दुर्गों से राज करके चारों ओर के सामन्तों को हुक्म देते थे।

panels.shot: medium shot profile of young Dantidurga
panels.action: A younger Dantidurga, in simpler armour and Rashtrakuta crest, bows before unseen overlords in a Chalukya audience hall, his eyes steady and reflective.

dialogue.text: Among those feudatories were the Rashtrakutas, old Deccan chiefs. Dantidurga began as their leading prince, a vassal under Chalukya suzerainty, owing tribute and troops.

i18n.hi: इन सामन्तों में राष्ट्रकूट भी थे, पुराने दक्कनी मुखिया। दंतिदुर्ग पहले उन्हीं के अग्रणी राजकुमार थे, चालुक्य अधिपत्य के अधीन एक जागीरदार, जो कर और सेना चुकाता था।

panels.shot: dynamic wide of cavalry on the move
panels.action: Dantidurga rides at the head of a Rashtrakuta cavalry column across dusty scrubland, banners streaming, elephants and infantry following under a glaring sun.

dialogue.text: But the Deccan was changing. Raiding, hiring, marching, Dantidurga gathered men and horses, binding tribal chiefs, peasant levies and mercenaries into a harder, faster army.

i18n.hi: पर दक्कन बदल रहा था। लूट, भर्ती और मार्च करते हुए दंतिदुर्ग ने लोगों और घोड़ों को जोड़ा, जनजातीय सरदारों, किसान पैदल और भाड़े के सैनिकों को गढ़कर तेज, कठोर सेना बनाई।

panels.shot: medium close-up on Dantidurga reading copper plates
panels.action: Inside a tent lit by lamplight, Dantidurga studies a set of freshly inscribed copper plates, their shining surfaces held by Brahmin scribes seated near him.

dialogue.text: At the same time, he drew Brahmins and scribes to his side. Gifts of land and copper plates bound ritual experts to Rashtrakuta fortunes, stitching alliances over fields and temples.

i18n.hi: साथ ही उसने ब्राह्मणों और लेखकों को खींच लिया। जमीन और ताम्रपत्र दान से उसने कर्मकांडियों को राष्ट्रकूट भाग्य से जोड़ा, खेतों और मंदिरों पर गठबंधन सिले।

panels.shot: wide shot of Ellora cliffs
panels.action: The basalt cliffs of Ellora rise in layered terraces, with scaffolds and workers around an emerging rock-cut temple, forests and a distant settlement visible below.

dialogue.text: At Ellora in the western Deccan, new shrines were hewn from living rock. Later, inscriptions in these caves would remember the Rashtrakutas, tying their name to this sacred landscape.

i18n.hi: पश्चिमी दक्कन के एलोरा में नए देवालय जीवित चट्टान से तराशे गए। बाद के अभिलेख इन गुफाओं में राष्ट्रकूटों को याद करेंगे, उनका नाम इस पावन भू‑दृश्य से जोड़ेंगे।

panels.shot: intense medium shot on Dantidurga conferring with Brahmins
panels.action: Dantidurga leans forward in a wooden pavilion, conferring with a small group of Brahmins who sit cross-legged, one pointing to a palm-leaf manuscript.

dialogue.text: To rule, force was not enough. Dantidurga listened as learned men spoke of dharma, sacrifice and the old Vedic rites that could make a man more than a mere warlord.

i18n.hi: राज करने को सिर्फ बल काफी नहीं था। दंतिदुर्ग ने पंडितों से धर्म, यज्ञ और उन प्राचीन वैदिक विधियों की बातें सुनीं जो किसी सेनानायक को साधारण से अधिक बना सकती थीं।

panels.shot: wide shot of rival powers at the frontier
panels.action: At a frontier river, two opposing camps face each other across the water—armies with different standards, while farmers watch anxiously from the banks.

dialogue.text: Around them, rival powers pressed. Gurjara-Pratiharas to the north-west, Pallavas and other southern courts watched the Deccan. The Chalukyas struggled to hold their network of feudatories together.

i18n.hi: इधर‑उधर से प्रतिद्वंद्वी ताकतें दबाव डाल रहीं थीं। उत्तर‑पश्चिम में गुर्जर‑प्रतिहार, दक्षिण में pallava और अन्य दरबार दक्कन को देखते थे। चालुक्य अपने सामन्तों के जाल को सँभालने में जूझ रहे थे।

panels.shot: dramatic oblique wide of battlefield
panels.action: On a hazy battlefield, Rashtrakuta warriors clash with a larger but disordered force; Dantidurga rides along the flank, signalling with his sword as dust swirls around the fighting lines.

dialogue.text: In that strain, Dantidurga moved. The Samangad plates recall his campaigns, telling of victories in the Deccan and beyond, as he broke the strength that had guarded the Chalukya throne.

i18n.hi: उसी तनाव में दंतिदुर्ग चला। सामंगढ़ ताम्रपत्र उसकी मुहिमें गिनते हैं, दक्कन और उससे परे की जीतें बताते हैं, जब उसने उस शक्ति को तोड़ा जो चालुक्य सिंहासन की रखवाली करती थी।

panels.shot: low-angle medium of Dantidurga after victory
panels.action: Dantidurga stands on a slight rise after battle, armour dusty, looking over retreating enemy banners in the distance, his officers gathering around him with wary respect.

dialogue.speaker: dantidurga
dialogue.text: The earth bows to none who cannot hold it. Now we must hold belief.

i18n.hi: धरती उसी की है जो उसे थाम सके। अब हमें आस्था भी थामनी होगी।

panels.shot: interior wide of a subdued Chalukya court
panels.action: The Chalukya hall is shown again, this time with fewer nobles, some seats empty, attendants looking uneasy as an unseen announcement is made.

dialogue.text: The last Badami Chalukya, Kirtivarman II, lost his power. The records fall silent on his fate, but not on the outcome: Rashtrakuta authority rose where Chalukya suzerainty had stood.

i18n.hi: आखिरी बादामी चालुक्य, कीर्तिवर्मन द्वितीय, ने अपनी शक्ति खो दी। उसका अंत लेखों में धुंधला है, पर नतीजा साफ है: जहां चालुक्य अधिपत्य था, वहां राष्ट्रकूट सत्ता उठ खड़ी हुई।

panels.shot: medium shot of Dantidurga with map and chiefs
panels.action: Dantidurga, now more richly dressed, stands over a floor map marked with stones; chiefs, farmers' headmen and Brahmins surround him, each watching as he places a token at the centre.

dialogue.text: Yet his victory was not only over a single king. It was the rise of a new centre in the western Deccan, a reweaving of military, agrarian and ritual networks under Rashtrakuta command.

i18n.hi: उसकी जीत सिर्फ एक राजा पर नहीं थी। यह पश्चिमी दक्कन में नए केन्द्र का उदय था, जहां सेना, खेती और कर्मकांड के जाल राष्ट्रकूट हुक्म के तहत फिर से बुने गए।

panels.shot: solemn interior wide of ritual enclosure preparation
panels.action: Beneath a temporary wooden pavilion, priests and artisans assemble a gleaming golden vessel shaped like a womb, while Dantidurga watches, hands folded, the fire altar unfinished beside it.

dialogue.text: To seal this change, Dantidurga chose a powerful rite. The Samangad copper plates call it the Hiranyagarbha—the golden womb—an ancient Vedic sacrifice of rebirth and sovereignty.

i18n.hi: इस बदलाव को मोहर लगाने को दंतिदुर्ग ने एक प्रबल अनुष्ठान चुना। सामंगढ़ ताम्रपत्र इसे हिरण्यगर्भ—स्वर्ण गर्भ—कहते हैं, जो पुनर्जन्म और राजसत्ता का प्राचीन वैदिक यज्ञ था।

panels.shot: close-up on artisans polishing the golden vessel with Dantidurga in background
panels.action: Hands of goldsmiths carefully polish the smooth inner surface of a golden cylindrical vessel, while in the blurred background Dantidurga stands silhouetted against the light.

dialogue.text: Artisans shaped the shining womb. The ritual would show him emerging as if from the primal golden egg from which, the hymns said, the cosmos itself had once unfolded.

i18n.hi: कारीगरों ने चमकता गर्भ गढ़ा। अनुष्ठान में वह ऐसे निकलेगा मानो उसी मूल स्वर्ण अंडे से, जिससे, ऋचाएँ कहती थीं, कभी सारा ब्रह्मांड फूटा था।

panels.shot: wide shot of gathered public around the ritual
panels.action: A large crowd of townsfolk, soldiers, village elders and Brahmins gathers around the ritual pavilion in the open air, all eyes turned toward the golden structure at its centre.

dialogue.text: This rite was no private devotion. People came from towns and fields, from temples and forts, to witness how their new lord would be publicly remade in the sight of gods and men.

i18n.hi: यह पूजा कोई निजी साधना नहीं थी। नगरों‑खेतों, मंदिरों‑किलों से लोग आए, देखने कि उनका नया स्वामी देवताओं और मनुष्यों के सामने कैसे फिर से गढ़ा जाएगा।

panels.shot: dramatic medium shot of Dantidurga entering the golden womb
panels.action: Stripped to a simple cloth and ornaments, Dantidurga stoops and steps into the upright golden vessel, priests chanting beside him, the sacrificial fire glowing nearby.

dialogue.text: On the appointed day, he set aside his armour. The Rashtrakuta prince lowered himself into the golden womb, while priests recited verses of creation and the air trembled with expectation.

i18n.hi: नियति दिन उसने कवच उतार रखा। राष्ट्रकूट राजकुमार स्वर्ण गर्भ में उतरा, पुरोहित सृष्टि सूक्त पढ़ते रहे, हवा में प्रतीक्षा का कंपन भर गया।

panels.shot: low-angle shot from inside the pavilion as Dantidurga emerges
panels.action: From the opened golden vessel, Dantidurga rises slowly, now wearing royal ornaments and a diadem, the firelight and morning sun catching on his form as the crowd strains forward.

dialogue.text: Then, before the assembly, he emerged. In that scripted moment, the vassal shed his older bonds. The Rashtrakuta Dantidurga stood as one ritually reborn, legitimised as king.

i18n.hi: फिर सभा के सामने वह निकला। उस रचे क्षण में जागीरदार ने अपने पुराने बंधन झाड़ दिए। राष्ट्रकूट दंतिदुर्ग यज्ञ‑जन्मा, विधिवत मान्य राजा बनकर खड़ा था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Brahmin announcing grant with copper plates
panels.action: A Brahmin holds up gleaming copper plates before the crowd, while Dantidurga sits behind him on a simple throne, hands resting on his knees, composed and attentive.

dialogue.text: The copper plates proclaimed it. They spoke of his conquests, of the Hiranyagarbha, and of lands granted to Brahmins, making the ritual and its benefits part of the official memory of his rise.

i18n.hi: ताम्रपत्रों ने सब घोषित किया। उन्होंने उसकी विजयों, हिरण्यगर्भ यज्ञ और ब्राह्मणों को मिली भूमिदानों का ब्योरा दिया, ताकि यज्ञ और उसके फल उसके उदय की राजकीय स्मृति बन जाएं।

panels.shot: wide shot of Ellora cave façade with royal presence
panels.action: In front of a newly carved Ellora cave façade, a sculpted panel of a royal figure is being finished by artisans, while Dantidurga and his retinue visit the site, gazing up at the work.

dialogue.text: At places like Ellora and Manpur, inscriptions would later tie the Rashtrakutas to temples and caves, etching their name into stone as well as onto copper and into ritual memory.

i18n.hi: एलोरा‑मानपुर जैसे स्थानों पर बाद के शिलालेख राष्ट्रकूटों को मंदिरों और गुफाओं से जोड़ेंगे, उनका नाम पत्थर, ताम्रपत्र और कर्मकांड की याद में एक साथ उकेरेंगे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Dantidurga in later years overlooking fields
panels.action: An older Dantidurga, dignified and calm, stands on a balcony above irrigated fields and a busy village, watching ploughs and bullocks move in ordered lines.

dialogue.text: His reign, brief in years, was long in consequence. By his time, the Rashtrakuta name meant more than a clan of warriors; it meant a Deccan kingdom grounded in fields, forts and rites.

i18n.hi: उसका राज थोड़े बरस चला, पर असर लंबा रहा। उसके बाद राष्ट्रकूट नाम सिर्फ योद्धा कुल नहीं रहा; वह खेतों, किलों और यज्ञों पर टिके दक्कनी राज्य का प्रतीक बन गया।

panels.shot: montage-style wide of later Rashtrakuta glory
panels.action: A composite scene shows later Rashtrakuta splendour—larger cavalry hosts, more elaborate temples, scribes at work—framed like echoes around a central image of the golden womb ritual.

dialogue.text: Later Rashtrakuta kings would expand this power, even reaching into north India. Yet their house stood on the foundations laid when Dantidurga joined conquest with copper plates and cosmic rebirth.

i18n.hi: आगे के राष्ट्रकूट सम्राटों ने इस शक्ति को बढ़ाया, उत्तर भारत तक हाथ बढ़ाया। पर उनका महल उन नींवों पर खड़ा रहा जो दंतिदुर्ग ने विजय, ताम्रपत्र और ब्रह्माण्डीय पुनर्जन्म को जोड़ते हुए रखी थीं।

panels.shot: closing wide shot of an old copper plate in a scholar's hands
panels.action: Modern hands gently hold an aged copper plate charter over a desk, its script catching the light, while a faint ghosted image of a ritual pavilion and golden vessel hovers behind.

dialogue.text: Today, the Samangad plates and Ellora inscriptions still speak. They remind us that power endures not only by the sword, but by the stories, rituals and records that make it seem rightful.

i18n.hi: आज भी सामंगढ़ ताम्रपत्र और एलोरा के लेख बोलते हैं। वे याद दिलाते हैं कि सत्ता सिर्फ तलवार से नहीं टिकती, बल्कि उन कथाओं, अनुष्ठानों और अभिलेखों से जो उसे न्यायोचित दिखाते हैं।

title_i18n.en: Dantidurga Steps Through the Golden Womb
title_i18n.hi: दंतिदुर्गा का कदम स्वर्ण गर्भ में

subtitle_i18n.en: A feudatory remakes the Deccan through steel, inscription and sacred rebirth
subtitle_i18n.hi: एक सामन्त ने लोहे, लेख और पवित्र पुनर्जन्म से बदल डाला दक्कन
